en: The Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī as Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Proclaimed Grandee, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
I prostrate to the Supreme Universal Wisdom, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—
whose mind is pure and peerless, whose supernormal powers are unimpeded and unprecedented,
who is well able to pervade the realms of the ten directions, and who transforms and delivers all sentient beings according to their faculties.
I prostrate to Mañjuśrī, the Great Guide, who skillfully removes the dust and grime of the mind;
his heart is already pure, and his body is adorned with immeasurable merit.
He extensively expounds the wondrous Dharma to deliver all beings—devas, nāgas, and powerful asuras alike—all of whom support his feet and pay him homage.
The mantra of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī is as follows:
Namo mañjughoṣāya | mahāvidyāsattvāya | mahākāruṇikāya | vidyābhāṣaṇāya ||
yogati snuṣa-vinaraṇāya tadyathā oṃ bu bu mahāmaṇi rucira-karapa vicitra mukta-nama āḥ.
ākarṣaya laḥkṛtaśrīra | paramasattvamocaka | tathāgataguhyadara | pravaradharmaratnamudrā-vijayam || 15 ||
